matched_finding.subcategory: Interval terminology in the first Results paragraph
matched_finding.description: Interval terminology in the first Results paragraph: The interval terminology is inconsistent in this paragraph: the Generation effects are labelled as $95\%$ Confidence Intervals / CI, while the Methods state that the models are Bayesian and use $95\%$ credible intervals, and the next sentence reports HPDIs. This leaves the intended posterior interval summary for these Generation effects unclear.
matched_finding.quote: Results confirm these predictions. The average wheel speed (calculated as $1 \mathrm{~m} /$ descent time) increased across generations (Generation $95 \%$ Confidence Intervals: (1.58, 9.02), mean $=5.37 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{h}$, Figure 2.A) while participants' understanding did not (Generation $95 \% \mathrm{CI}$ : ( $-0.54,0.25$ ), mean $=-0.04$, Figure 2.B). The average wheel speed produced by first generation participants on their last trial was $123.6 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{h}$ ( $95 \%$ Highest Posterior Density Interval: (117.3, 130.6)) and their understanding score was 4.60

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: Absolute estimation vs comparative judgment — must know these tap different constructs
ground_truth.original_snippet: Participants’ understanding was evaluated by presenting them with pairs of wheels that differed in their configurations, and asking them to predict which wheel would reach the bottom of the rails first.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: Participants’ understanding was evaluated by presenting them with pairs of wheels that differed in their configurations, and asking them to estimate how long each wheel would take to reach the bottom of the rails.
ground_truth.description: Changed from comparative judgment (which wheel first) to absolute estimation (how long) — measures different construct; absolute timing requires calibrated knowledge, not relative understanding

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: All-previous vs last-two configurations — must understand information parity in transmission chain designs

ground_truth.modified_snippet: Participants could consult all of their previous configurations between any trials.
ground_truth.description: Changed from last-two to all-previous configurations — breaks information parity with between-generation transmission, confounding cumulative cultural learning with individual data accumulation

matched_finding.subcategory: Overclaim about mixed-gender settings in discussion
matched_finding.description: Overclaim about mixed-gender settings in discussion: The discussion overstates external validity here: the experiment used sex-segregated, sequential chains of isolated individual participants, so the paper does not directly support the claim that the findings generalize to mixed-gender collaborative settings.

Instead they mainly produce unidimensional models related to a specifically salient dimension 18. Although evidence of individual' erroneous theories of motion are sometimes considered as experimental artefacts resulting from impoverished stimuli

ground_truth.difficulty_rationale: 'Well-understood' directly contradicts next sentence about 'absence of explicit understanding'
ground_truth.original_snippet: The cultural niche hypothesis suggests that complex technologies like bows result from the accumulation of many, mostly small, often poorly understood improvements made across generations linked by cultural transmission 1,9,14.
ground_truth.modified_snippet: The cultural niche hypothesis suggests that complex technologies like bows result from the accumulation of many, mostly small, well-understood improvements made across generations linked by cultural transmission 1,9,14.
ground_truth.description: Changed 'poorly understood' to 'well-understood' — fundamentally mischaracterizes the hypothesis; contradicts next sentence about 'absence of explicit understanding'

matched_finding.subcategory: Tension in the cultural-niche framing of improvements
matched_finding.description: Tension in the cultural-niche framing of improvements: In the opening theoretical framing, the phrase “well-understood improvements” is in tension with the next sentence’s claim that optimization can arise “in the absence of explicit understanding.” Since the paper’s contrast between causal-reasoning and cultural-transmission accounts turns on whether improvements require causal understanding, this wording makes the cultural-niche mechanism harder to parse.
matched_finding.quote: The cultural niche hypothesis suggests that complex technologies like bows result from the accumulation of many, mostly small, well-understood improvements made across generations linked by cultural transmission 1,9,14. Over time, the selective retention of improvements gives rise to highly optimized solutions in the absence of explicit understanding about how these solutions work.

ground_truth.description: Added explicit model selection based on data fit, contradicting the pre-registration claim that 'analysis plan took place before any data were collected'

matched_finding.subcategory: Model selection sits uneasily with “Preregistered” label
matched_finding.description: Model selection sits uneasily with “Preregistered” label: Analysis 1 is labeled preregistered, but the final model specification is said to have been selected by comparing candidate models fitted to the observed data. Unless the candidate set and selection criterion were themselves preregistered, this makes the confirmatory status of the reported model unclear.
matched_finding.quote: Preregistered analysis 1 investigated the average speed of wheels across generations in the Configurations treatment. Data were restricted to participants' last two trials in order to limit the occurrence of wheels that did not descend in the dataset. We fitted a linear model with "Speed" as the outcome variable, "Trial", "Generation" as predictor variables and "Player's identity" and "Chain's identity" as random effects (see Supplementary Table 1 for model output). The final model specification was selected after comparing several candidate models based on fit to the observed data.

ground_truth.description: Deleted specification that failed wheels got speed=0 — without this, reader can't evaluate if increasing speed reflects genuine optimization or just fewer failures
